p: The crime-family saga every other crime story is secretly copying. Slow burn, total masterpiece.
The rare sequel that might beat the original. Two timelines, one family, zero mercy.
A prison story about hope that will absolutely wreck you, in the best way.
Three cops, one murder, 1950s Hollywood glamour hiding total rot. Twisty and so cool.

t: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
p: One rebel vs. the most quietly terrifying nurse in movie history. You'll be furious, and you'll love it.
Deserts so huge your screen becomes a window. Epic is not a strong enough word.
A comedy about the end of the world, starring the dumbest smart people ever put in charge of anything.
Mozart as a giggling rock star, told by the jealous rival plotting his downfall. Opulent and wicked.
The blueprint for every adventure movie since. Whips, snakes, face-melting. Perfect.
A haunted-cabin movie that turns into a slapstick cartoon halfway through. Gross, hilarious, iconic.
Kubrick's most notorious: dazzling, disturbing, and definitely a watch-with-Dad one.
The western every director steals from. Gorgeous, and way darker than old movies look.
Two con men build the perfect scam. The most fun you will ever have being lied to.
A surveillance expert hears something on a tape he really shouldn't have. Quiet, paranoid, unforgettable.
One sheriff, a town full of cowards, and a train arriving at noon. Real-time tension in 85 minutes.
Dinosaurs brought back to life. Still the best blockbuster ever built. The kitchen scene!
Gritty cops chase a smuggling ring through 1970s New York, with the wildest car chase ever filmed.
The true story of a killer who taunted the newspapers, and the people the puzzle slowly consumed.
Two brothers who barely know each other, one cross-country road trip. A performance you have to see.
A kidnapping scheme goes hilariously, horribly wrong in the snowiest, politest place on Earth.
A hunter finds two million dollars in the desert. What comes after him is the scariest villain ever. Call it.

t: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
p: The aliens arrive, and instead of a war it's wonder. The ending is pure goosebumps.
A newsman snaps on live TV and becomes a ratings hit. Somehow predicted the entire internet in 1976.
Crime stories told out of order, with the coolest dialogue ever written. Iconic does not cover it.
A genius janitor and a stubborn therapist. Four words from this one will live in your head forever.
A lonely cab driver slides into obsession in neon-soaked 1970s New York. Intense and heavy.
A man stuck at his window becomes convinced he watched a murder. You will be leaning at your screen.
A loan shark decides the movie business is just crime with better lunches. Effortlessly cool.
An insurance man, a dangerous woman, a plan for the perfect crime. The granddaddy of every noir.
A getaway driver who times every heist to his playlist. Car chases choreographed like music videos.
Seven warriors defend a helpless village. The original team-up movie, and still the best.
A teacher who makes poetry feel dangerous. Carpe diem. Bring tissues.
A detective pulls one small thread and unravels an entire city. The gold standard of movie mysteries.
A haunted house in space, except the ghost has acid for blood. Ripley is the blueprint for every hero since.
Warriors chase each other across rooftops and treetops like gravity is optional. Gorgeous and sweeping.
A kung fu movie crossed with a Looney Tunes cartoon. You will laugh out loud, guaranteed.
Shaolin monks apply kung fu to soccer. Exactly as glorious as that sounds.
A writing student, his monstrous momma, and a very bad plan borrowed from a Hitchcock movie.
Steve Martin invents the modern dumb-genius comedy. He hates these cans!
Two kids trying to survive wartime Japan. The most beautiful sad movie ever animated. You will cry.
A SWAT team fights its way up thirty floors of a criminal high-rise. The purest action movie ever made.
A lonely kid befriends the strange girl next door. A vampire story that is secretly about friendship.
A dying bureaucrat decides to do one thing that matters before he goes. Quietly life-changing.
A deep-sea rig crew meets something glowing at the bottom of the trench. Cameron, underwater, all-in.
One crime, four completely different versions of the truth. Invented a whole way of telling stories.
Locked in a room for 15 years, released, given five days to figure out why. Jaw on the floor. Ask Dad first.
A hard-boiled detective story where every noir archetype is a high schooler. From the Knives Out guy.

t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
p: What if you could erase someone from your memory? A sci-fi love story that hits like a truck.
A gentle man with a dark past befriends a boy who needs a friend. Mmm-hmm.
What if reality is a simulation and you just found out? Changed action movies forever. Red pill time.
An oil man's ambition swallows everything in its path. I drink your milkshake! Towering.
A man who cannot form new memories hunts a killer, told backwards. Your brain will do a flip.
A rich man's ransom dilemma becomes a citywide manhunt. Kurosawa doing a crime thriller. Perfect.
A wandering samurai plays two gangs against each other for fun and profit. Cool, distilled.
New apartment, friendly neighbors, something very wrong. Dread turned up one degree at a time.
No child has been born in 18 years. Then, a miracle. Contains shots you won't believe are possible.
A girl escapes a brutal war into a fairy tale that is just as dangerous. Dark, gorgeous, unforgettable.
The motel, the shower, the twist everyone knows, and it STILL works. The grandmother of all horror.
Neon rain, android hunters, and the question of what makes us human. The look of all sci-fi since.
A club of kids discovers Dracula has assembled a monster team in their town. Goonies with real monsters.
Four friends walk the train tracks one summer. About being twelve, in the best and saddest way.
The Oz sequel that is basically a horror movie. Wheelers. A hall of screaming heads. Unforgettable.
A crime movie that takes a hard left turn at sundown. Best watched knowing absolutely nothing.
An insomniac, a soap salesman, and a club with one rule. The twist gets studied in film schools.
A billionaire's birthday gift: a game that invades his entire life. Is any of it real?
Two detectives, seven deadly sins, one rain-soaked city. Grim, gripping, and THAT ending.
A private detective follows a mystery film reel into some very dark corners. Heavy one. Ask Dad first.
A kidnapping plan built from good intentions goes completely, tragically wrong. No mercy in this one.
She spent thirteen years in prison planning something immaculate. Icy, stylish revenge.
A one-hit-wonder band's entire rise and fall, plus the catchiest song ever written for a movie.
Suburban dads convince themselves the creepy new neighbors are murderers. Peak weird Tom Hanks.
A 1950s bad-boy musical that is also making fun of 1950s bad-boy musicals. Johnny Depp, full cheese.
Suburban house, staticky TV, they're heeere. The friendly-faced nightmare classic.
Growing up inside Rio's most dangerous neighborhood, shot like lightning. Unforgettable.
The sequel nobody expected to be a masterpiece. Huge, gorgeous, melancholy sci-fi.
Five criminals meet in a police lineup. Home of the most famous rug-pull ending in movies.
The midnight-movie musical. Costumes, callbacks, the Time Warp. A whole culture, not just a film.
A two-hour chase across the apocalypse with practical stunts and a flame-throwing guitar. Witness it.
Five strangers, one Saturday detention. The teen movie every teen movie descends from.
Not about winning the fight. About going the distance. You will want to run up some stairs after.
Before the sequels got silly: a lean, sad thriller about a veteran pushed one step too far.
An empty hotel, a frozen maze, REDRUM. Possibly the scariest movie ever made. Ask Dad first.
Two brothers on a mission from God, with a car-chase budget that nearly leveled Chicago. And the MUSIC.
A young FBI trainee has to interview the most charming monster in movies. Keep the lights on.
Scientists get fired and start a ghost-removal business in New York. Comedy blockbuster perfection.
The sequel swaps haunted house for war movie. Get away from her! Ripley forever.
One barefoot cop, one skyscraper, the best villain of the eighties. Yes, it is a Christmas movie.
Giant underground worms vs. one small desert town. The perfect fun monster movie.
Are you not entertained? A betrayed general fights his way back through the Colosseum.
The opening twenty minutes changed war movies forever. Brutal, moving, essential.
The robot from the first movie is back, and this time he's on your side. Best action sequel ever.
From cavemen to the stars. Less a movie, more an experience. Trust it and go with it.
A teen, a DeLorean, and 1955. The tightest script ever written. A perfect movie. Start here.
A cab driver picks up his worst fare ever: a silver-haired hitman on a one-night schedule. LA at night.
Wrong man, cross-country chase, a crop duster, Mount Rushmore. The first action blockbuster.
Poker, debts, and reading exactly what the other guy is holding. Sneaky-great.
A documentary about a guy who WILL finish his horror movie no matter what. Hilarious, then moving.
A grumpy file clerk becomes a comic-book legend by writing about his boring life. True story.
A screenwriter gets so stuck he writes himself into the movie you are watching. Total brain candy.
The fake documentary about the world's loudest band. These go to eleven.
A mockumentary about deranged dog-show people. Every single line is quotable.
Small-town musical theater meets Broadway-sized delusion. Painfully, perfectly funny.
Two teens get zapped into a black-and-white 1950s sitcom, and color starts leaking in.
A case of mistaken identity ruins a rug and spirals gloriously out of control. The Dude abides.
Put on the sunglasses. OBEY. CONSUME. A sci-fi satire with the longest fistfight ever filmed.
The babysitter, the mask, the theme music. Invented the slasher movie. Still scary.
A nearly abandoned police station under siege all night long. Lean, mean Carpenter.
Antarctic crew, shape-shifting alien, total paranoia. Greatest practical effects AND ending ever. Ask Dad.
Manhattan is a maximum-security prison and Snake Plissken has 22 hours. The coolest eyepatch in cinema.
Two sarcastic best friends graduate and start drifting apart. For anyone who has ever felt too weird.
A murder at an English manor, upstairs and downstairs, everyone with secrets. Knives Out's grandparent.
There is a tiny door behind a filing cabinet that leads into an actor's head. Go in.
A fifteen-year-old goes on tour with a rock band for Rolling Stone. Based on a true story. Pure joy.
A boxer who can take any punch except the ones to his pride. Devastating black-and-white Scorsese.
One guy just wants to get home. New York refuses to let him. Anxiety as comedy.

t: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou
p: A washed-up ocean documentarian hunts the shark that ate his friend. Deadpan and secretly lovely.
A family of former child geniuses and their terrible, charming dad. Sad and funny in the same frame.
The real women's baseball league of World War II. There's no crying in baseball!
A mother builds an empire for a daughter who deserves none of it. Classic noir with big feelings.
A hitman and his son on the run in 1931. Every single frame looks like a painting.
An amnesiac, an actress, and Los Angeles folding in on itself like a dream. Don't solve it. Feel it.
Fog rolls in, there are things inside it, and the supermarket becomes the real horror. THAT ending.
His best friend just... stops liking him. On a tiny Irish island. Funny, then quietly devastating.
Two hitmen hide out in a fairytale Belgian town. Much funnier and much sadder than that sounds.
Wrongly convicted, on the run, hunted by a marshal who does not care. I didn't kill my wife!
The most ambitious fifteen-year-old alive goes to war with a grown man. Wes Anderson's breakout.
A teacher tries to stop one relentless overachiever from winning class president. Savage comedy.
A bank robbery goes wrong immediately and becomes a live TV circus. True story. Attica!
A paperwork dystopia vs. one clerk's daydreams of flying. Gilliam's weird, wonderful masterpiece.
A French car thief and an American girl in Paris. Invented cool. Invented the jump cut.
Two schemers realize a flop can make more money than a hit, so they stage the worst show ever written.
A teenage con artist poses as a pilot, a doctor, and a lawyer while the FBI chases him. Mostly true!
Old Wolverine, one last road trip. A superhero movie that is secretly a western. Bring tissues.
A fourteen-year-old girl hires the meanest marshal alive to hunt her father's killer. She runs the show.
Aliens arrive and a linguist has to figure out how to talk to them. Then it becomes something much bigger.
A shy Parisian secretly fixes strangers' lives. Possibly the most charming movie ever made.
A wife vanishes and her husband's smile looks wrong. Trust absolutely no one in this movie.
A genius mathematician's brilliant, unraveling mind. The turn in the middle lands hard.
A broken soldier finds honor in a vanishing world. Sweeping battles, quiet heart.
The perfect bank heist, where nothing is what the cops think it is. Every rewatch reveals more.
Two rival magicians destroy each other over one impossible trick. Are you watching closely?
A man starts hearing a narrator describing his life, and she is planning his death.
One kidnapper, twenty-three personalities. McAvoy is astonishing. Stay for the last scene.
A stoner detective wades through a case even he cannot follow. Vibes-first noir.
Two lonely Americans wide awake in the middle of Tokyo. Quiet, funny, and glowing.
Two engineers build something impossible in a garage. The hardest time-travel plot ever. Take notes.
London, completely empty. The infected are FAST. The movie that rebooted zombies.
A superhero show shot like a fever dream. From the Fargo showrunner, X-Men adjacent, gloriously unhinged.
The xenomorph finally reaches Earth. New, creepy, and from the same brain as Legion and Fargo.
New crimes, new snow, same universe as the movie. Every season is its own complete story.
A chemistry teacher breaks bad. The most acclaimed show ever made, and it earns every bit of it.
The lawyer's story. Slower burn than Breaking Bad, and somehow it might be even better.
Three neighbors start a true-crime podcast about a murder in their own building. Cozy, clever, funny.
The original summer blockbuster. You will hear two notes of cello and feel genuine fear. Still perfect.
As far back as anyone can remember, the most electric crime movie ever made. Scorsese at full power.
One kid, one fake sick day, one borrowed Ferrari. The most charming movie about skipping school ever.
Fencing, fighting, revenge, giants, miracles, true love. As you wish. Perfect from minute one.
One man lives the same day forever until he gets it right. Funny, then sneakily profound.
Cops and thieves as mirror images, De Niro across a table from Pacino, and the loudest shootout ever filmed.
A treasure map in the attic, a gang of misfits, booby traps. The adventure every kid deserves. Hey you guys!
Hitchcock's strangest obsession: a detective, a mystery woman, and a spiral you fall into with him.
What if your whole life was a TV show and everyone knew except you? Made in 1998, more true every year.
As if! Jane Austen's Emma reborn in 90s Beverly Hills. Endlessly quotable, secretly smart.
Shakespeare's Taming of the Shrew in a 90s high school, plus young Heath Ledger serenading the bleachers.
The anthropology of high school, written by Tina Fey. On Wednesdays we wear pink. So fetch.
A senior year of fighting with your mom because you are exactly alike. Funny and quietly devastating.
Being seventeen and certain everyone else has it figured out. Painfully funny because it is true.
A small-town girl secretly joins a roller derby team. Scrappy, joyful, and criminally underrated.
You know exactly how it ends and it still wrecks you. Romance and spectacle at maximum possible scale.
A girl wanders into a bathhouse for spirits and must work to free her parents. Pure imagination, start to finish.
Forest gods versus iron town, and no easy villains anywhere. Miyazaki's fierce, gorgeous epic.
A young witch starts a delivery business in a seaside town. The coziest movie ever animated.
Anyone can wear the mask. The most visually inventive superhero movie ever made, and the most heartfelt.
A boy, a giant robot, and a choice: you are who you choose to be. Superman. Bring tissues.
A door to a world where your Other Mother has buttons for eyes. Beautiful and properly creepy.
Wes Anderson does Roald Dahl in stop-motion corduroy. A cussing delight for the whole family.
One poor family infiltrates one rich family, job by job. First subtitled film to win Best Picture. Flawless.
The true unsolved case that haunted Korea, from the Parasite director. That final shot stays with you.
A laundromat owner discovers every life she could have lived. Googly eyes, hot-dog fingers, Best Picture, big feelings.
A meet-the-parents weekend goes very, very wrong. The sunken place. Horror with something to say.
Something is hiding in the clouds above a horse ranch. A UFO movie about why we cannot look away.
A dead novelist, a scheming family, one great detective, a donut hole in the donut's hole. The modern whodunit.
A drummer and the teacher who terrorizes him toward greatness. Not quite my tempo. Heart-pounding.
The invention of Facebook told as a knife fight in dialogue form. Fincher plus Sorkin. Endlessly rewatchable.
An astronaut is left for dead on Mars and decides to science his way out. Funny, smart, gripping.
A young coder is flown in to test whether a beautiful robot is truly conscious. It gets chilly in there.

t: Monty Python and the Holy Grail
p: The knights of the Round Table vs. a killer rabbit, taunting Frenchmen, and coconut horses. Quote it forever.
Mel Brooks does the monster movie better than the monster movies did. It's pronounced Fronkensteen.
A disaster movie where every single line is a joke. Surely you can't be serious. Don't call me Shirley.
A slacker fights the zombie apocalypse with a cricket bat and a plan that mostly involves the pub. Perfect.
A supercop gets exiled to a sleepy English village where accidents keep happening. The greater good.
To date Ramona, Scott must defeat her seven evil exes, video-game style. A comic book come alive.
The board game as a slamming-doors farce with three different endings. Flames, on the side of my face.
Washed-up sci-fi actors get recruited by aliens who thought their show was real. By Grabthar's hammer.
A fake substitute teacher turns a prep-school class into a rock band. Jack Black's finest hour.
A Brooklyn lawyer with zero trial experience defends his cousin in small-town Alabama. The two yutes.
Vote for Pedro. Deadpan small-town weirdness that sneaks up on you and becomes strangely beautiful.
A reformed robber and a police officer steal a baby. There were five! The Coens at their most cartoon-alive.
Homer's Odyssey in Depression-era Mississippi with the best soundtrack ever recorded. We thought you was a toad.
The greatest musical ever made, about Hollywood learning to talk. Joy, distilled into 103 minutes.
One juror votes not guilty and slowly turns the other eleven. One room, 96 minutes, total grip.
A broke screenwriter moves in with a forgotten silent-film star. Dark, glamorous, and an all-timer.
Postwar Vienna, a dead friend who might not be dead, and the greatest character entrance in movies.

t: Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid
p: The two most charming outlaws in the West, one step ahead of the posse. Newman and Redford, again.
A slasher movie about people who have seen slasher movies. Scary AND funny. What's your favorite scary movie?
A boy who sees dead people, and the doctor trying to help him. You think you know the twist. Watch it anyway.
Three rules: no bright light, no water, never feed them after midnight. Guess what happens. A Christmas movie.
A recently deceased couple hires a chaotic bio-exorcist to scare off the living. Say it three times.
Zombies on a bullet train, and a distracted dad trying to get his daughter home. Thrilling, then heartbreaking.
Lola has twenty minutes to save her boyfriend, and three tries to get it right. 81 minutes of pure adrenaline.
Two revolutionaries, one legendary bromance, physics fully optional. The most maximalist action musical ever.
A boy, a projectionist, and a lifetime of movies in a small Sicilian town. Wait for the kisses reel. Tears.

wq: The King of Kong: A Fistful of Quarters
p: Two grown men battle for the Donkey Kong world record. More dramatic than it has any right to be.
Climbing 3,000 feet of Yosemite granite with no rope. Your palms will sweat for the entire runtime.
Your work self and your home self are surgically separated. What is your job hiding? Eerie and addictive.
A human lie detector drives across America solving murders. Columbo energy, from the Knives Out guy.
One perfect season, 1980, and everything true about being a teenager. Everyone is in it before they were famous.
Kids, bikes, a missing friend, and something from the Upside Down. All of Dad's 80s movies in one show.
The FBI agents who invented criminal profiling by interviewing monsters. Fincher-cold and riveting.
Rod Serling's original anthology. Twenty-five minutes, one twist, decades ahead of everything since.
Star Wars for grown-ups: how a rebellion actually gets built. The best writing in the galaxy.
Two sisters on opposite sides of a city at war. The most beautiful animation ever put on television.
A mixed-race swordmaster hunts four men through Edo Japan. Kurosawa DNA, jaw-dropping animation.
Two brothers lost in an autumn forest that is not quite right. Two hours total. Watch it in October.
Howard Hughes builds planes, movies, and an empire while his own mind quietly betrays him. Scorsese, huge.
A cannibal western with a weirdly jaunty banjo score. Grisly, funny, completely one of a kind. Ask Dad first.
A billionaire and a photographer survive a plane crash in the wilderness. Then the bear shows up.
The buddy-cop movie every buddy-cop movie copies. One partner is too old for this, the other is unhinged.
Commandos in the jungle slowly realize something is hunting THEM. Get to the choppa. Action perfection.
Wes Anderson's scrappy first heist, before the symmetry kicked in. Seventy-five-year plan included.
A thief accidentally becomes an actor, then accidentally becomes a detective. Narrated with total disrespect.
A bruiser-for-hire and a hopeless private eye stumble through 1977 Los Angeles. Relentlessly funny.

t: The Adventures of Buckaroo Banzai Across the 8th Dimension
wq: The Adventures of Buckaroo Banzai Across the 8th Dimension
p: A rock-star neurosurgeon particle physicist fights aliens from the 8th dimension. Exactly that weird. Cult forever.
A river journey deeper into the war and the dark. Napalm in the morning. Overwhelming, in the best way.
An escaped convict and the boy he takes hostage form the bond neither of them had. Quietly devastating.
Tarantino's first: a heist gone wrong, told entirely in the aftermath. Color-coded criminals, killer soundtrack.
A flight attendant calmly plays every side of a money-smuggling scheme. Tarantino's coolest, most grown-up movie.
The retired gunslinger takes one last job, and the whole legend of the West falls apart. The final word on westerns.
A masked revolutionary takes on a fascist Britain. Remember, remember the fifth of November.
A grumpy retiree, his Hmong neighbors, and one immaculate car. Starts as get-off-my-lawn, ends up enormous.
Detectives, long cases, longer memories. Season one is a swampy all-timer; Night Country is a chiller.
Two FBI agents chase aliens, monsters, and conspiracies. Mulder and Scully forever. The truth is out there.

wq: The Outsider Stephen King HBO series
p: An open-and-shut murder case, except the suspect was provably in two places at once. Stephen King, slow dread.
A cursed New England island town where the supernatural keeps showing up like weather. Scary-funny and brand new.
Ten thousand people live in an underground silo, forbidden to ask what's outside. Naturally, someone asks.
A small-town detective with a heavy life works one devastating case. Kate Winslet. All-timer miniseries.
